definitions.explanation: Describes performing an action with notable skill or cleverness. Can convey positive admiration for technique or a negative nuance of cunning manipulation, depending on context.

examples.japanese: {言葉|ことば}を{巧|たく}みに{使|つか}う。
{彼|かれ}は{質問|しつもん}を{巧|たく}みにかわした。
{詐欺師|さぎし}は{巧|たく}みな{手口|てぐち}で{人々|ひとびと}を{騙|だま}した。
examples.english: The swindler deceived people with clever tricks.

notes:
The adverbial form of {巧|たく}み (na-adjective meaning skillful/clever). Describes actions performed with notable skill or cleverness. Can be used both positively (impressive skill) and negatively (cunning manipulation).

USAGE:
When used with neutral or positive verbs, it praises skill and dexterity. When used with verbs like {騙|だま}す (to deceive) or かわす (to dodge), it implies craftiness or cunning.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {巧|たく}みに{操|あやつ}る: to manipulate skillfully
- {巧|たく}みに{使|つか}う: to use skillfully
- {巧|たく}みにかわす: to dodge deftly
- {巧|たく}みな{技|わざ}: skillful technique
- {巧|たく}みな{話術|わじゅつ}: skillful way of speaking

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {上手|じょうず}に: skillfully — the everyday, neutral word for doing something well
- {器用|きよう}に: deftly — emphasizes manual dexterity or versatility
- {巧|たく}みに: adds a literary quality and can imply cleverness or cunning that the others lack
